full_judgment:
6. Mr. T.H. Khan, learned Counsel with Dr. A.K.M. Ali, Advocate, appearing for the respondent No.1 submitted that the Courts below believed the case of the plaintiff and after elaborate discussion and assigning cogent reasoning’s arrived at certain findings and the High Court Division under revisional jurisdiction had no scope to interfere with it. The learned Counsel further submitted that the interference is not warranted when the concurrent findings of fact do not suffer from any legal infirmity as in the present case; that the main point to be looked into in this matter is whether Dag Nos. 1642 and 1643 as mentioned in the impugned kabalas were sold to the defendant or to see whether it was the intention of the plaintiff to sell the plots in Dag Nos.1646 and 1647, which are disputed questions of fact and the Courts below after perusal of the khatians, mouza, map, the report of the Advocate Commissioner after local inspection and after taking into consideration the evidence of witnesses, came to concurrent findings. He pointed out that the local inspection was held for the identification of the suit land and the deposition of the plaintiff and the defendant witnesses relates to the possession of the suit land and P.W. 1-8 categorically supported the case of the plaintiff regarding his possession on the suit and but on the other had D.W. 1 made no specific assertion about the possession, D.W.2 being a caretaker of the defendant and interested witness was not believed by the Courts below and D.W.3 also could not identify the suit land. 

 9. It appears from the record that both the Courts below held that the plaintiff and Haji Abdur Raquib acquired a plot in Dag No.1642 by way of jote settlement from one Indu Bhushan Dhar and others and got their names recorded in the Khatian and got a plot in Dag No.1643 by way of purchase and got their names recorded in Khatian by filing the Objection Case No.416 of 1962 and both of them became owners to the extent of 8 annas share each and Abdur Raquib sold his 8 annas share of both the plots in Dag Nos. 1642 and 1643 to the plaintiff verbally on 15.12.1960 followed by delivery of possession and then executed a kabala on 09.06.1989 in support of the earlier sale and thus lost his interest in the suit land. The Court of appeal below specifically found that Haji Abdur Raquib's presence was not necessary in the suit.
